q-107987.name: Question 1
q-107987.problem:
Find the characteristic equation of the matrix 
$B=[\begin{aligned}8 & 0 \\ 6 & -5\end{aligned}].$
q-107987.worked_solution:
First, we find the matrix $\,B-\lambda I:$
﻿﻿﻿

$$
B-\lambda I=[\begin{aligned}8-\lambda  & 0 \\ 6 & -5-\lambda \end{aligned}].
$$

Then, the characteristic equation is

$$
\begin{aligned}det(B-\lambda I) & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}8-\lambda  & 0 \\ 6 & -5-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (8-\lambda )(-5-\lambda )-6\cdot 0 & =0 \\ -40-8\lambda +5\lambda +{\lambda }^{2} & =0 \\ {\lambda }^{2}-3\lambda -40 & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

q-76342.problem: Find the characteristic equation of the matrix $M=[\begin{aligned}\sqrt{3} & \sqrt{7} \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}].$
q-76342.worked_solution:
First, we find the matrix $\,M-\lambda I:$
﻿﻿﻿

$$
M-\lambda I=[\begin{aligned}\sqrt{3}-\lambda  & \sqrt{7} \\ 0 & 1-\lambda \end{aligned}].
$$

Then, the characteristic equation is

$$
\begin{aligned}det(M-\lambda I) & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}\sqrt{3}-\lambda  & \sqrt{7} \\ 0 & 1-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (\sqrt{3}-\lambda )(1-\lambda )-0\cdot \sqrt{7} & =0 \\ (\sqrt{3}-\lambda )(1-\lambda ) & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

q-106954.problem: Find the characteristic equation of the matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ 2 & 4\end{aligned}].$
q-106954.worked_solution:
First, we find the matrix $\,A-\lambda I:$
﻿﻿﻿

$$
A-\lambda I=[\begin{aligned}1-\lambda  & -2 \\ 2 & 4-\lambda \end{aligned}].
$$

Then, the characteristic equation is

$$
\begin{aligned}det(A-\lambda I) & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}1-\lambda  & -2 \\ 2 & 4-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (1-\lambda )(4-\lambda )-2\cdot (-2) & =0 \\ 4-\lambda -4\lambda +{\lambda }^{2}+4 & =0 \\ {\lambda }^{2}-5\lambda +8 & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

q-107982.name: Question 6
q-107982.problem:
Find all real eigenvalues of the matrix 
$P=[\begin{aligned}1 & 4 \\ 2 & 3\end{aligned}].$
q-107982.worked_solution:
Let's start by writing the matrix $P-\lambda I:$
﻿﻿﻿

$$
P-\lambda I=[\begin{aligned}1-\lambda  & 4 \\ 2 & 3-\lambda \end{aligned}]
$$

Now, let's find and solve the characteristic equation $det(P-\lambda I)=0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}det(P-\lambda I) & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}1-\lambda  & 4 \\ 2 & 3-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (1-\lambda )(3-\lambda )-2\cdot 4 & =0 \\ 3-\lambda -3\lambda +{\lambda }^{2}-8 & =0 \\ {\lambda }^{2}-4\lambda -5 & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Using the quadratic formula, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\lambda  & =\frac{4\pm \sqrt{(-4)^{2}-4\cdot 1\cdot (-5)}}{2\cdot 1} \\  & =\frac{4\pm \sqrt{36}}{2} \\  & =\frac{4\pm 6}{2} \\  & =5,-1.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the eigenvalues are $\lambda =-1$ and $\lambda =5.$

q-12293.problem:
Find all real eigenvalues of the matrix 
$P=[\begin{aligned}-5 & 1 \\ 1 & -5\end{aligned}].$
q-12293.worked_solution:
Let's start by writing the matrix $P-\lambda I:$
﻿﻿﻿

$$
P-\lambda I=[\begin{aligned}-5-\lambda  & 1 \\ 1 & -5-\lambda \end{aligned}].
$$

Now, let's find and solve the characteristic equation $det(P-\lambda I)=0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}det(P-\lambda I) & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}-5-\lambda  & 1 \\ 1 & -5-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (-5-\lambda )(-5-\lambda )-1\cdot 1 & =0 \\ 25+5\lambda +5\lambda +{\lambda }^{2}-1 & =0 \\ {\lambda }^{2}+10\lambda +24 & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Using the quadratic formula, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\lambda  & =\frac{-10\pm \sqrt{{10}^{2}-4\cdot 1\cdot 24}}{2} \\  & =\frac{-10\pm \sqrt{4}}{2} \\  & =\frac{-10\pm 2}{2} \\  & =-6,-4.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the eigenvalues are $\lambda =-6$ and $\lambda =-4.$

q-36781.problem:
Find all real eigenvalues of the matrix
$U=[\begin{aligned}-7 & 5 \\ -1 & -7\end{aligned}].$
q-36781.worked_solution:
Let's start by writing the matrix $U-\lambda I:$
﻿﻿﻿

$$
U-\lambda I=[\begin{aligned}-7-\lambda  & 5 \\ -1 & -7-\lambda \end{aligned}].
$$

Now, let's find and solve the characteristic equation $det(U-\lambda I)=0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}det(U-\lambda I) & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}-7-\lambda  & 5 \\ -1 & -7-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (-7-\lambda )(-7-\lambda )-5\cdot (-1) & =0 \\ 49+7\lambda +7\lambda +{\lambda }^{2}+5 & =0 \\ {\lambda }^{2}+14\lambda +54 & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Computing the discriminant of the quadratic equation above, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}D & ={14}^{2}-4\cdot 1\cdot 54 \\  & =196-216 \\  & =-20 \\  & <0.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that the characteristic equation does not have real solutions and therefore $U$ does not have real eigenvalues.

Find all real eigenvalues of the matrix M=[1317012].

a
λ=13 and λ=17
b
λ=13 and λ=12
c
λ=17 and λ=12
d
There are no real eigenvalues
e
λ=17 (double root)
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Let's start by writing the matrix M−λI: ﻿﻿﻿M−λI=[13−λ17012−λ]

Now, let's find and solve the characteristic equation det(M−λI)=0:

det(M−λI)=0|13−λ17012−λ|=0(13−λ)(12−λ)−0⋅17=0(λ−13)(λ−12)=0

Therefore, the eigenvalues are λ=13 and λ=12.

Note: The eigenvalues of a triangular (or diagonal) matrix are the entries on the main diagonal.
